Then news of deceit arrived from Constantinople,
to the effect that they wished to set up another emperor.
Therefore, Emperor Manuel returned in haste to Constantinople,
and the plan which they had devised came to naught.
And in that same year, in the month of Nisan, there was a flood in Baghdad,
and the waters destroyed part of the walls of the Caliph's palace.
And the people fled to the western side, carrying the sick, the old women, and the children upon their shoulders,
because the wrath [of God] terrified them.
And the fare of a small boat reached
for a single crossing
four gold dinars.
And in the year 1471
of the Greeks [1160 AD],
when the son of Joscelin, who was held prisoner, used to go forth continually from Ḥārim and raid the territory of Aleppo,
an ambush was set for him by Nur al-Din, and he was captured,
and he was cast into the pit where his father had been placed.
And in that same year,
which is the year 555
of the Arabs [1160 AD],
on the second of their third month [Rabi' I],
in the month of Adar,
the Caliph al-Muqtafi died of the disease of quinsy,
and his son al-Mustanjid reigned after him.
After al-Muqtafi, his son al-Mustanjid [reigned] twelve years.
When his father died,
he arose to enter where the deceased was laid.
Now the wife
of his father,
that is to say, the mother of his younger brother, who was a Turkish woman,
prepared her handmaids,
and they took knives and made ready,
so that when al-Mustanjid entered, they would kill him,
in order that the kingdom might belong to her younger son.
Then one of them went out and informed him.
And he gathered the executioners,
and subdued his brother,
and bound him and imprisoned him.
And he also came upon these women,
and he shut up each one {OCR?} of them aside,
and he killed whomever he wished.
And the caliphate was confirmed to him,
and he was proclaimed.
And in the year 1472
of the Greeks [1161 AD],
Sir Amalric, the brother of the King of Jerusalem, entered the land of Egypt,
and the Franks swept away great wealth and departed.
And shortly after, al-Fa'iz,
the Caliph of Egypt, died.
And on this account, the Egyptians agreed to give the Franks an annual tribute of one hundred and sixty thousand gold dinars.
